mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off channel, depressing near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening episodes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS increase is not followed by >1% SPX decline within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while PAYEMS < INDPRO for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market weakening detected by dual indicators
failure_condition: In similar labor weakening regimes, the 20-day forward return is positive or statistically indistinguishable from baseline (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a 12-month moving average reflects strengthening construction activity and supports optimism in the business cycle, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows with similar HOUST momentum, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, while inflation pressures (CPIAUCSL) remain elevated, suggests supply-side bottlenecks persisting into the near term and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 12-month moving average while CPIAUCSL > 230
failure_condition: In analogous supply-constrained regimes, the 20-day forward return is positive or not significantly different from baseline (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for three consecutive months indicates a strong labor market, prompting the Fed to remain accommodative and supporting equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar strong-labor regimes are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in monthly retail employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 jobs without a corresponding rise in industrial payrolls (PAYEMS > INDPRO) signals demand-driven labor absorption, forecasting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 while PAYEMS > INDPRO in the same month
failure_condition: In analogous demand spikes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for two consecutive months, amid low interest rate expectations (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%), suggests disinflation is entrenched and supports risk-on positioning, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5%
failure_condition: In similar disinflationary regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average, without a corresponding decline in housing starts (HOUST), suggests sector-specific supply disruptions that weigh on equities over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 12-month moving average while HOUST remains above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In comparable supply disruptions, the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.2).
